text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Trend of job reduction over past years reversed due to shorter working hours, rising sales and acquisitions. (p1)
- Dutch business forecast investment will rise by 28 percent this year to 19 billion guilders, according to CBS. (p1)
- Sharply falling pork prices sparked panic among investors on Amsterdam's agricultural futures market late last week. (p1)
- Philips Electronics will shed 5,500 jobs this year, according to trade union Industriebond FNV. (p3)
- PTT Telecom plans to offer customers speech telephony calls via internet next year. (p3)
- Spice Girl music sales boost Polygram shares.(p15)
VOLKSKRANT
- EU close to settling French demands and thus reach agreement on stability pact. (p1)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Chipknip consortium are making inroads into entertainment sector with their computer smartcards, leaving behind the rival Chipper group. (p15)
- Philips shows sharp growth in mobile phone market. (p15)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch economy to reach growth of 3.75 percent next year, a record for this parliamentary term, according to Central Plan Bureau (p1).
- Minister of Social Affairs Ad Melkert demands return of money from Health Minister Els Borst after too few jobs created in health sector. (p1)
- Coordinated action between Dutch, French and Belgian police over weekend leads to at least 55 arrests of drugs suspects. (p5)
TROUW
- Dutch railways can be held liable for long delays to passengers, according to public transport commission. (p9)
